notes:
Smarter next-episode continuity, safer auto-skip, and playback failures that finally tell you what went wrong.

NEXT EPISODE KEEPS YOUR EXACT RELEASE. Reelm now reads the bingeGroup token addons attach to a stream - the protocol's own marker for 'these are the same release series'. Where an addon sends one (Torrentio and most of its derivatives do), continuing into the next episode is release-exact rather than inferred from the release title. Addons that do not send one lose nothing: the existing matching is unchanged and still carries those.

TORRENT PICKS PREFER A HEALTHY SWARM. Among next-episode candidates that are otherwise identical - same addon, same quality, same release - Reelm now prefers more seeders, then the larger file. These only ever break a tie. A 720p with 200 seeders will never win over your 1080p with 20, and another addon will never win just by having more peers.

AUTO-SKIP NO LONGER TRUSTS AN OUTRO THAT IS NOT AT THE END. A mislabelled chapter, an anime insert song, or a community timestamp made against a different cut could previously seek you past content you had not watched. An outro that leaves a substantial amount of episode after it is now ignored for both auto-skip and the Next Episode hand-off.

SKIP INTRO FOR ANIME OPENED THROUGH CINEMETA. Anime with an ordinary IMDb id can now reach AniSkip, through a per-season mapping matched on the season itself rather than on position in a list. Split-cour seasons deliberately keep the old behaviour instead of guessing a mapping that could be wrong.

FAILED STREAMS NOW SAY WHY. A dead link used to look exactly like a slow one - an endless spinner. Reelm now names the cause: expired, removed, refused, rate limited, or unplayable on this device. It still never switches source on its own; that stays your call.

SMOOTHER REMOTE ON TV. Holding a direction on the remote no longer floods the app with focus work. Single presses are completely unaffected.
